'''''Narcissus papyraceus''''' (from ''[[papyrus]]'' and ''aceus''; meaning paper-like<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dictionary of Botanical Epithets |url=https://botanicalepithets.net/dictionary/dictionary.137.html |access-date=2024-04-28 |website=botanicalepithets.net}}</ref>), one of a few species known as '''paperwhite''', is a [[perennial]] [[bulb|bulbous plant]] native to the [[Mediterranean]] region, from [[Greece]] to [[Portugal]] plus [[Morocco]] and [[Algeria]]. The species is considered naturalized in the [[Azores]], [[Corsica]], [[Texas]], [[California]] and [[Louisiana]].<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=281955 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref> The white flowers are borne in bunches and are strongly fragrant. It is frequently grown as a [[house plant]], often forced to flower at [[Christmas]].

Paperwhites are part of the genus ''Narcissus'' which includes plants known as [[daffodil]]s.

==Description==
The stems are mid-green and grow upright. Mature height is usually 1–1.5 ft (30–45 cm), though this varies by variety. Several white flowers are borne at the top of each stem and are strongly scented.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Curtis, William |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/14314 |title=Curtis's botanical magazine |last2=Curtis |first2=William |last3=Hooker |first3=Joseph Dalton |last4=Hooker |first4=William Jackson |last5=Prain |first5=D. |last6=Stapf |first6=O. |last7=Trust |first7=Bentham-Moxon |last8=Trust |first8=Bentham-Moxon |last9=Royal Botanic Gardens |first9=Kew |date=1806 |publisher=Academic Press [etc.] |volume=v.23-24=no.881-966 (1806) |location=London}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
Many cultivars are available and are easy to force into bloom indoors. Unlike other ''Narcissus'' species, paperwhites do not require chilling to promote bloom. The bulbs begin to grow as soon as they are planted, with flowers appearing in 3–4 weeks.

''Narcissus papyraceus'' thrives in moist, peat moss based potting mix. Plants can also be grown in containers of water. Cool temperatures between {{convert|50|–|65|F|C}} and indirect light will help to prolong the bloom time.<ref>{{cite web|title=Paperwhite Bulbs|url=http://www.whiteflowerfarm.com/paperwhite-bulbs-holiday.html#}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Guide to Paperwhites|url=http://www.southernliving.com/home-garden/gardens/guide-to-paperwhites-forcing-bulbs-planting-and-tips}}</ref>
